title: Microsoft Purview: auto-labeling policies will cover legacy .doc, .xls and .ppt files
summary: The briefing accurately distinguishes the planned legacy-format rollout from the formats currently listed in Learn. The notice supports the edit-and-rerun requirement, and the cited documentation supports the policy controls, licensing and operational prerequisites.

claims.claim: Microsoft plans service-side auto-labeling support for legacy Word .doc files.
claims.quote: Microsoft Purview server-side auto-labeling will support legacy Microsoft Office file formats, including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: Microsoft plans service-side auto-labeling support for legacy Excel .xls files.
claims.quote: including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: Microsoft plans service-side auto-labeling support for legacy PowerPoint .ppt files.
claims.quote: including Word (.doc), Excel (.xls), and PowerPoint (.ppt).

claims.claim: An encrypting label used with SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling must use Assign permissions now.
claims.quote: When the auto-labeling policy includes locations for SharePoint or OneDrive, the label must be configured for the Assign permissions now setting

claims.claim: An encrypting label used with SharePoint or OneDrive auto-labeling must set User access to content expires to Never.
claims.quote: User access to content expires must be set to Never.

claims.claim: New and modified files are included using the current policy settings.

claims.claim: Auditing must be turned on for auto-labeling simulation.
claims.quote: Auditing is turned on for Microsoft 365. Required for simulation.

claims.claim: Sensitivity labels must be enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive.
claims.quote: Sensitivity labels are enabled for Office files in SharePoint and OneDrive. Required before any label can be applied to files in those locations.

claims.claim: A label's scope must include Files & other data assets to label files.
claims.quote: To label files, the label scope must include Files & other data assets.

claims.claim: Auto-labeling is not available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.
claims.quote: Auto-labeling isn't currently available in all regions because of a backend Azure dependency.

claims.claim: The Auto-labeling page is not visible in the Purview portal if the tenant cannot support the functionality.
claims.quote: If your tenant can't support this functionality, the Auto-labeling page isn't visible in the Microsoft Purview portal.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Turn on policy enables enforcement.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... When you're ready to run the policy without simulation, select the Turn on policy option.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Mode Enable enables policy actions.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the auto-labeling policy that you want to modify. ... The Mode parameter specifies the action and notification level ... Enable: The policy is enabled for actions and notifications.

claims.claim: The documented Purview policy route followed by Edit policy and Choose locations where you want to apply the label reaches location selection.
claims.quote: select the Edit policy option at the top of the page, from either tab. ... For the page Choose locations where you want to apply the label: Select and specify locations for Exchange, SharePoint, and OneDrive.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -AddSharePointLocation <SharePointSiteLocation> adds included SharePoint sites.
claims.quote: The AddSharePointLocation parameter specifies the SharePoint sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the SharePointLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter adds OneDrive locations.
claims.quote: The AddOneDriveLocation parameter specifies the OneDrive sites to add to the list of included sites when you aren't using the value All for the OneDriveLocation parameter. You identify the site by its URL value.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies > policy > Edit policy reaches the policy editor.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Solutions > Information Protection > Policies > Auto-labeling policies. ... Select your policy ... For policy in the Simulation section, select the Edit policy option at the top of the page, from either tab.

claims.where: controls[2].api; Governance controls table; Open questions
claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy -Identity <AutoLabelingPolicyName> -Comment <text> edits the policy comment.
claims.quote: Use the Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy cmdlet to modify auto-labeling policies in your organization. ... The Comment parameter specifies an optional comment.

claims.claim: Purview portal > Audit > Start recording user and admin activity turns on auditing.
claims.quote: Select the Audit solution card. ... Select the Start recording user and admin activity banner.

claims.claim: Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true turns on auditing.
claims.quote: Run the following PowerShell command to turn on auditing. ... Set-AdminAuditLogConfig -UnifiedAuditLogIngestionEnabled $true

claims.claim: The auditing command is run in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Complete the following steps to turn on auditing by using Exchange Online PowerShell: 1. Connect to Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: Turning auditing on or off requires the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online.
claims.quote: You must be assigned the Audit Logs role in Exchange Online to turn auditing on or off.

claims.claim: Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in Security & Compliance PowerShell.

claims.claim: TestWithoutNotifications places the policy in test mode without actions or notifications.
claims.quote: TestWithoutNotifications: An audit mode where no actions are taken, and no notifications are sent (Test mode).

claims.claim: It is not stated whether the PowerShell comment edit restarts the legacy-format crawl in the same way as the notice's policy edit.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview auto-labeling legacy Office files PowerShell Comment restart crawl; "Set-AutoSensitivityLabelPolicy" "legacy" "Comment". Opened the cmdlet and auto-labeling pages. StartSimulation restarts simulation; no legacy-format crawl guarantee found.
